page_title: AI pair programming in your terminal

sources.entry: Aider - AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo #free

summary.name: Aider
summary.one_liner: Aider is an AI pair programming tool that runs in your terminal, letting you work with LLMs to build new projects or edit an existing codebase in a local git repo.
use_cases: Building a new project with an LLM
Adding features or fixing bugs in an existing codebase
Reviewing and undoing AI-made code changes via git
Running linters and tests automatically on AI edits
Giving an AI screenshots or docs as context for code work
Editing code from inside an IDE using comments
summary.what_it_does: Aider lets you pair program with LLMs in the terminal on a new project or an existing codebase. It builds a map of your entire codebase to work in larger projects and supports many popular languages such as Python, JavaScript, Rust, Ruby, Go, C++, PHP, HTML and CSS. It automatically commits changes with sensible commit messages so you can use normal git tools to diff, manage, and undo AI edits. It can also take images and web pages as chat context, accept voice requests, and automatically lint and test code after each change. The page says it works best with Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek, OpenAI o1, o3-mini and GPT-4o, and can connect to almost any LLM, including local models.
notable: Automatically commits AI changes with descriptive git commit messages
Builds a map of the entire codebase for larger projects
Can fix problems reported by linters and test suites after each change
Works with most LLMs including local models, best with APIs
caveats: Works best with LLM API keys, which the user must supply; the web chat mode requires copy/pasting code back and forth
Pricing is not stated on the page; the directory listing tags it as free
